conventions.convention: Knots are smooth and oriented in standard oriented S³. TOP concordance uses locally flat annuli with product end collars; exotic concordance uses smooth annuli in boundary-marked manifolds homeomorphic to S³×I. Localized concordance uses smooth R_n-homology products, with R_n=Z[1/|n|].

Satellites use preferred zero framings. Strong winding ±1 means normal generation of the closure-complement group by the solid-torus meridian; it is stronger than ordinary winding ±1. Satellite operators are initially set maps.

With first-loop-first concatenation, the normal-cover right coefficient system transports around a based loop a by left multiplication by its quotient image g⁻¹. Its deck action induces conjugation u↦a⁻¹ua on the covering subgroup's abelianization.

Intersection and linking pairings use the supplied parallel standard Hermitian structure, are conjugate-linear in the first variable and right-linear in the second, and use the induced boundary orientation.

Fraction-field first-homology vanishing defines the linking form but does not alone imply nonsingularity. The nonsingularity conclusion additionally requires a componentwise principal-right-ideal, vanishing-H₀, or cyclic-image condition.
For winding n, the pattern cobordism identifies meridian classes by [μ_K]=n[μ_P(K)], rather than literal equality; n is a unit over R_n.

The analytic signature and final rank conclusions assume full AC. The signature defect is L² signature minus ordinary signature; independence of bounds is a separate theorem, including an explicitly external closed-TOP signature input.
The finite-prime signature functions use the first-variable positive-push Seifert matrix, assign signature zero at 1, and give normalized own-prime mean 4N_i/p_i. The primes are distinct and odd.

load_bearing.statement: For the supplied initial V with H₁(V;Z)=Z, H₂(V;Z)=Z^(2r), height-s integral zero/unit pairs, finite marked standard adjunctions, and a PTFA coefficient map whose restriction to V factors through π/π^(s), the image pairs retain their identities and the localized boundary-intersection cokernel dimension is at most its ordinary dimension, which is at most 2r. Every boundary component with nontrivial restricted map has vanishing localized H₁ and isotropic inclusion kernel. The result applies to the supplied topological and smooth manifolds without choice.

For a compact connected oriented collared topological four-manifold with the stated involutive coefficient inclusion R⊆K and standard unitary system, m zero/unit intersection pairs and localized boundary-cokernel dimension at most 2m imply that the linking form vanishes on the inclusion kernel of any selected connected boundary component with H₁(M₀;K)=0. No vanishing condition is imposed on the other boundary components.

The stated closure-slice hypotheses give weak injectivity in the corresponding localized, exotic, TOP, or conditionally standard smooth category. From P(K)=P(J), the auxiliary reduction constructs R with R(−K#J)=U, ribbon closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K), and w(R)=w(P); strong winding is retained when P has it.

For the stated closed connected oriented three-manifold with marked H₁=Z generator and fixed infinite-cyclic coefficient convention, the integral, rational and prime linking forms are defined on the whole respective first homology modules. Their actual coefficient values agree through the rational quotient map and the specified primitive-annihilator reduction map. Every nonzero integral self-value remains nonzero rationally and modulo all primes outside an explicit finite set.

For the supplied winding-zero smooth infection and any commutative field k, both boundary inclusions identify the classical first homology modules with H₁(E;k[t,t⁻¹]). Their induced comparison is an isometry and carries the based axis class to the actual companion-meridian class.
Assume full AC. For a closed oriented three-manifold M and a fixed homomorphism to Γ, any two compact oriented four-dimensional bounds extending that homomorphism have equal L²-signature defects.

For a supplied finite list of distinct odd primes p_i and positive heights C_i, finite disk-band knots have nonnegative signature functions with values 2N_i>C_i at the selected primitive pair, zero at all other selected roots, own-prime mean 4N_i/p_i, and zero cross-prime means, without choice.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.2 says the classes are rationally independent because 'a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation.' Clearing denominators initially gives an integer combination that is torsion modulo the filtration, rather than necessarily zero there. One must also multiply by its finite order before applying the excluded-integer-relation argument. The smooth supplier thm-smooth-winding-zero-iterates-have-infinite-rank-in-every-quotient explicitly includes this torsion-clearing step in Proof 2.1–3.1. The same short justification applies to the TOP argument here.

seams_checked.note: This is a contextual page prerequisite. The assigned proofs establish their required localization and Alexander-module claims separately; they do not strengthen a twisted-torsion theorem or assert its converse.

The satellite definition preserves the supplied tube, meridian, preferred-longitude and winding conventions. No essentiality or incompressibility conclusion is inferred from the definition, and no reverse implication is used.

Smooth and locally flat categories, end collars, reverse-mirror inverses and choice qualifications are distinguished. Uses of the stronger AC_ω group theorem in unqualified CDR results are explicitly replaced by the stated finite-input argument.

This is contextual prerequisite metadata. The signature-bump branch supplies its own exact finite matrix calculation and geometric realization; it does not infer a knot realization or concordance conclusion from an unstated converse of algebraic classification.
No assigned proof invokes Fox–Milnor factorization as a sufficient sliceness criterion. The page edge supplies background rather than an additional proof premise.

TOP geometric inputs are explicitly identified as external where used. The CDR proof separates topological standardness from conditional smooth standardness; it does not infer smooth sliceness from a TOP conclusion.

The opened coefficient suppliers distinguish defined linking forms from nonsingularity, supplied TOP half-pair data from smooth solutions, and canonical cyclic defects from independently defined rho invariants. The assigned consumers retain these qualifications; the closed TOP comparison is separately declared and agrees with Lück–Schick Theorem 0.2.
